subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Evidence-linked grouping of generic runtime objects: vtable install/reset and scalar-deleting-destructor conventions, vtable-driven UI widget lifecycle/dispatch, resource destructors (Bink/font), iterator/multi-list container teardown, linked-list manipulation, and small geometric helpers.

summary: Wave-06 packet covering 29 generic runtime-object functions. Four structural conventions recur: (1) vtable pointer installed/reset at this+0x0, either at construction (0x0048FEB0) or restored during teardown (0x0048D3E0, 0x0048FD80, 0x0048E0D0, 0x0048E360, 0x00495300, 0x0048C0D0); (2) the MSVC scalar-deleting-destructor shape (run teardown body, then free the object iff (a2 & 1) != 0, return this) seen in 0x0048CA30, 0x0048E0B0, 0x0048FE90, 0x004952E0, 0x004902A0 and the in-body variant 0x0048FD80; (3) vtable-slot-driven UI widget behavior (change signal at obj+0x2C, dispatch slot at obj+0x40, child dispatch list at this+0xE0/0xE8/0xEC, scroll/counter value via obj+0xB4) shared by 0x0048D4B0, 0x0048D590, 0x0048F300, 0x00490640, 0x00490660, 0x0048EA60; and (4) container teardown walking arrays/linked lists and releasing nodes via FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00490B90, 0x00491740, 0x00491770, 0x00495300). Most concrete class identities remain UNKNOWN; the classes proposed here are DERIVED groupings of functions that demonstrably share field offsets and vtable slots, and equal offsets on different objects (e.g. this+0xE0 as scroll value vs child-list head vs stored path) are NOT merged.

function_roles.role: vtable_reinstall_helper: restores object vtable at this+0x0 to off_5ABF88 then delegates to an unresolved sub-call; runs inside a destruction/reset sequence.
scalar_deleting_destructor_wrapper: runs LinkedListDestructor teardown then frees object iff (a2 & 1) != 0; returns this.
vtable_reset_and_base_teardown: resets vtable at this+0x0 to off_5AC1D0 then runs base teardown sub_485EB0 (unresolved); used in destructor sequences.
scroll_progress_handler: normalizes scroll value to 0..1 and maps it to a thumb pixel position through vtable slots +24/+32/+44/+56/+176/+180; refreshes when the position changes.

input_dispatch_navigation: scans short input codes, treats 203 as previous and 205 as next, increments/decrements the selection (integer field this+0xE0 or vtable+0xB4 counter) and signals the change via vtable slot +0x2C.
scalar_deleting_destructor_wrapper: runs media-player teardown body 0x0048E0D0 then frees object iff (a2 & 1) != 0; returns this.

media_player_destructor: resets vtable to off_5AC3E0, closes/frees the Bink handle at this+0xE0 via ConditionalFreeWithBinkClose when non-null, frees the secondary allocation at this+0xE8, then delegates to base teardown sub_485EB0.

font_resource_destructor: resets vtable to off_5AC490, closes/frees the Bink handle at this+0xE4 via ConditionalFreeWithBinkClose when non-null, frees the secondary allocation at this+0xFC, then delegates to base teardown (ObjectInitWithVTableCleanup).

directory_change_handler: appends self to a doubly linked list, compares current path (this+0xB8) with stored path (this+0xE0) defaulting to byte_5EA438, copies the new path on mismatch and fires the vtable+0xAC notification, then always refreshes via vtable+0x2C.
point_in_rect_hit_test: returns 1 when point (a2,a3) is strictly inside the axis-aligned rect with origin this+0x14/this+0x18 and extent this+0xC/this+0x10; used by mouse/position hit testing.
state_reset_with_conditional_virtual_dispatch: zeroes byte flags this+0x17D/0x17E; when state this+0x104 != 4 resets it to 0 and dispatches vtable+0x40 with argument 0.
ui_control_destructor: restores vtable to off_5A443C, conditionally frees the child resource pointer at this+0x4, then frees the object itself when (a2 & 1) is set; returns this.
scalar_deleting_destructor_wrapper: runs vtable/teardown init 0x0048FEB0 then frees object iff (a2 & 1) != 0; returns this.
vtable_init_constructor_helper: installs vtable off_5AC6B0 at this+0x0 then delegates remaining init to sub-initializer sub_485EB0.
conditional_teardown_with_vtable_notification: runs LinkedListDestructorWithVTableNotification teardown then frees object iff (a2 & 1) != 0; returns this.
vtable_dispatch_init: dispatches the vtable+0x40 method with argument 0, then iterates the child dispatch list and returns its result.

child_dispatch_list_iteration: walks the child linked list (head this+0xE0, count this+0xEC) and dispatches each child's vtable method at offset 16 with a bool derived from ShortComputation_6720; returns the child count.

multi_list_destructor: destroys the 16-byte element array (count this+0x0, pointer this+0x8) and three embedded singly-linked lists (this+0xC, this+0x1C, this+0x2C), freeing array block and nodes; returns 0.
broadphase_filter_scan: iterates a singly-linked list (head this+0x0, cursor this+0x8) applying the sub_491680 filter to each node AABB quad; returns 1 on first match else 0.
conditional_multi_list_destructor: when the object pointer at this+0x0 is non-null, destroys it via MultiListDestruction and frees it via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
destroy_all_iterators: destroys every list iterator in the container reached through *this (count obj+0x0, array obj+0x8) plus two embedded iterators; returns the final destruction result.
conditional_resource_cleanup: when the flag byte this+0x8 is non-zero and the pointer this+0x0 is non-null frees the embedded pointer; then frees self iff (a2 & 1) != 0; returns this.

line_segment_rect_clip: clips a 2D line segment against an axis-aligned rect whose width/height come from a1+28/+32, clamping and interpolating per axis; returns whether the clipped line retains non-zero extent.
scalar_deleting_destructor_wrapper: runs track-database teardown body 0x00495300 then frees object iff (a2 & 1) != 0; returns this.

track_database_destructor: restores vtable to off_5AC998, destroys interior list containers and the segment list (this+0x18AC) and curve/section list (this+0xF0), frees several heap regions (this+0x1558, this+0x3C, four-slot run), walks the child-object list at this+0x4 invoking per-node vtable destructors, and zeroes the list heads.
field_getter: reads the DWORD at this+0x1570 and returns it unchanged; used by UIScreenSelectionHandler.

sum_tree_values_with_recursion: sums ShortComputation_5920 over the linked list seeded by FieldGetter_8e30, then adds ShortComputation_8f60(a1) and a recursive TreeWalkerVirtualCallRecurse result; returns -1 when a1 is null.
doubly_linked_list_node_unlink: splices node a2 out of a doubly linked list with head this+0x14 and tail this+0x18, fixing node next (+0x64) and previous (+0x68) links.

list_tail_pop_and_render_dispatch: pops the tail node of the render list (head this+0x14, tail this+0x18), unlinks it, dispatches its rectangle fields via GuardedSubRectangleRenderDispatch, and clears the node links.

classes.name: UIWidgetBase
classes.responsibility: DERIVED grouping of vtable-managed UI widget lifecycle/dispatch functions that share a vtable pointer at this+0x0, a state byte/flag region at this+0x104/0x17D/0x17E, a child dispatch list at this+0xE0/0xE8/0xEC, a rectangle region at this+0xC/0x10/0x14/0x18, and vtable dispatch slots +0x2C (refresh/change) and +0x40 (state dispatch). Construction/deconstruction both funnel through the shared base teardown sub_485EB0 (address not in packet).

classes.name: ScrollListControl
classes.responsibility: DERIVED grouping of scroll-bar / list-navigation UI control functions that share the selection/scroll value at this+0xE0, a storage-mode byte at this+0xF0, range bounds at this+0xF4/0xF8, and vtable slots +0x18/+0x20 (area extents), +0x2C (change signal), +0xA4 (post-update callback), +0xB0 (refresh), +0xB4 (mutable value pointer getter).

fields.name: selection_or_scroll_value
fields.type_guess: int or float depending on mode flag

classes.name: DirectoryChangeHandler
classes.responsibility: Object that registers itself into a doubly linked list and refreshes its directory-path buffer (this+0xB8) when the stored path (this+0xE0) changes, firing a vtable+0xAC notification and always refreshing via vtable+0x2C.

classes.name: ControlBase
classes.responsibility: UI control object whose destructor restores its vtable (off_5A443C) and conditionally releases a child resource pointer at this+0x4 before self-free.

classes.name: BinkVideoPlayer
classes.responsibility: Media player object holding a Bink video resource handle at this+0xE0 and a secondary heap allocation at this+0xE8; its destructor resets the vtable (off_5AC3E0), closes the Bink handle, frees the secondary allocation, and delegates to base teardown sub_485EB0.

classes.name: FontResourceObject
classes.responsibility: Font resource object holding a Bink video resource handle at this+0xE4 and a secondary heap allocation at this+0xFC; its destructor resets the vtable (off_5AC490), closes the Bink handle, frees the secondary allocation, and delegates to base teardown ObjectInitWithVTableCleanup.

classes.name: MultiListContainer
classes.responsibility: Container object holding an array of 16-byte list elements (count this+0x0, array this+0x8) plus three embedded singly-linked lists (heads this+0xC, this+0x1C, this+0x2C) and a trailing region at this+0x3C; fully destroyed by MultiListDestruction (0x00490B90), conditionally via 0x00491740.

classes.name: IteratorArrayContainer
classes.responsibility: Container reached through a pointer-to-pointer that owns an array of 16-byte list iterators (count obj+0x0, array obj+0x8) plus two embedded iterators, all destroyed by DestroyAllIterators.

classes.name: BroadphaseList
classes.responsibility: Singly-linked list object used for collision/broadphase filtering: head at this+0x0, iteration cursor at this+0x8, nodes carrying an AABB coordinate quad tested by the sub_491680 filter.

classes.name: TrackDatabase
classes.responsibility: GUESS-named object whose destructor (0x00495300) is the only packet member; it is a large container holding child objects (list at this+0x4), a curve/section list (this+0xF0), a segment list (this+0x18AC), interior list containers and several heap regions. The 'track database' semantics come from the packet's ABI lead name and are not independently proven.

classes.name: RenderQueueList
classes.responsibility: Doubly linked render list with head at this+0x14 and tail at this+0x18, whose nodes carry next/previous links at +0x64/+0x68; supports node unlink (0x00495A20) and tail-pop with rectangle render dispatch (0x00495AE0).

state_machines.name: StateResetGate
transitions: state != 4 -> reset state to 0 and dispatch vtable+0x40 with argument 0
state == 4 -> no reset, no dispatch (gate closed)

interfaces.name: VTableChangeSignal
interfaces.purpose: Vtable slot at offset +0x2C used to signal a content change / request refresh; shared by scroll/list navigation, directory-change handling and widget refresh paths.

interfaces.name: ScalarDeletingDestructor
interfaces.purpose: MSVC scalar-deleting-destructor convention: run the teardown body then free the object memory if and only if the low bit of the flag argument is set; return this. Applies to every 'DestructorWithConditionalFree' wrapper in this packet.

interfaces.name: BinkResourceLifetime
interfaces.purpose: Objects owning a Bink video resource handle close and free that handle (via ConditionalFreeWithBinkClose) during destruction, alongside a secondary heap allocation, before delegating to the base teardown.

compatibility_contracts.name: VtablePointerAtOffsetZero
compatibility_contracts.description: Every object in this subsystem stores its active vtable pointer at this+0x0. Construction installs the class vtable there (0x0048FEB0, off_5AC6B0); destruction restores the class vtable before running teardown (off_5AC1D0, off_5AC3E0, off_5AC490, off_5A443C, off_5AC998, off_5ABF88). A replacement must keep the vtable slot at offset 0 and reinstall the original vtable at the start of each destructor.

compatibility_contracts.name: ScalarDeletingDestructorFlagBit0
compatibility_contracts.description: All scalar-deleting-destructor wrappers free the object memory if and only if the low bit (a2 & 1) of the deletion-flag argument is set; the teardown body runs unconditionally first and the original this pointer is returned. A replacement must preserve this convention for callers that invoke deleting-destructors.

compatibility_contracts.name: UIWidgetVtableSlotIndices
compatibility_contracts.description: UI widget objects dispatch behavior through fixed vtable slots: +0x2C change/refresh signal, +0x40 state dispatch, +0xAC directory-change notification, +0xB0 refresh, +0xB4 mutable value getter, +0xA4 post-update callback, +0x18/+0x20 area-extent getters, and child dispatch method at offset +0x10 on child vtable. A replacement UI system must keep these slot indices stable.

compatibility_contracts.name: UIChildDispatchListLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: UI widget children are stored in a linked list with head at this+0xE0 and count at this+0xEC; each node holds the child object at node+0x0 and the child's dispatch method is at child-vtable+0x10. A replacement must reproduce this walk for child dispatch.

compatibility_contracts.name: BinkResourceReleaseOnDestruct
compatibility_contracts.description: Objects that own a Bink video resource handle must close and free it (via ConditionalFreeWithBinkClose) during destruction, and also free the secondary heap allocation, before the base teardown runs.

compatibility_contracts.name: MultiListContainerLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The multi-list container holds an array of 16-byte elements (count this+0x0, pointer this+0x8, with a 4-byte count header preceding the block) and three embedded singly-linked lists at this+0xC, this+0x1C, this+0x2C whose nodes carry a value at +0x0, next at +0x4 and a flags byte at +0x8. Destruction must drain the array (in reverse) and every list, freeing each node.

compatibility_contracts.name: RenderListHeadTailOffsets
compatibility_contracts.description: The doubly linked render list keeps head at this+0x14 and tail at this+0x18; node links live at node+0x64 (next) and node+0x68 (previous). Unlink and tail-pop must maintain head/tail and splice links so the tail marker stays consistent.

unresolved: Concrete class identity is UNKNOWN for most objects: off_5ABF88 (HUD timer vtable), off_5AC1D0/off_5AC6B0 (widget vtable), off_5AC3E0 (media player), off_5AC490 (font resource), off_5A443C (control base) and off_5AC998 (track-database) are not resolved to named types by this packet.

The shared base teardown sub_485EB0 (called by 0x0048D3E0, 0x0048FEB0, 0x0048E0D0, 0x0048E360) has no address in this packet; its contract is unverified and it cannot be cited as a callee evidence ref.
0x0048C0D0 delegates to VTableSetterSubCall_b4e0 whose address is absent from the packet; the call target cannot be cited.
Global dword_8AFE64 appears in static analysis of 0x0048E0D0 and 0x0048E360 but not in their raw bodies; role unconfirmed.

flt_59E440 and flt_59E450 (listed as accessed by 0x0048D4B0) are not directly referenced in the raw source; the mapping to the 0.0 / 0.5 constants (ZeroThreshold / DegreesToRadians per existing analysis) is not adopted here. flt_59E440 is used as the zero threshold by 0x00494C80.

Offset this+0xE0 carries three different meanings across different object bases: selection/scroll value (ScrollListControl), child-list head (UIWidgetBase) and stored path (DirectoryChangeHandler). They are kept as separate fields in separate classes per the equal-offset rule; the packet does not prove common ownership.
The storage-mode byte at this+0xF0 and the pointer-mode counter via vtable+0xB4 in 0x0048D590 are inferred from two parallel mutation paths, not fully classified.
Semantics of input codes 203/205 as previous/next navigation come from existing analysis, not independently proven.
The vtable+0x40 dynamic target, the meaning of state constant 4 (0x0048F300) and the meaning of the ShortComputation_6720 range 3..5 flag (0x00490660) are not resolvable from this packet.
The purpose of the unused parameter a2 in 0x00491280 is unknown; sub_491680's filter semantics are caller/callee-defined.
The null branch of 0x00491740 returns an uninitialized result variable, a decompiler artifact of a compiler-proven-unreachable path.

In 0x00495AE0 the node offset +100 (0x64) serves as both the next link and a tail-marker flag; its exact meaning is not confirmed, and roles of this+0x1C/0x20/0x24/0x28/0x78/0x7C/0x80/0xE4 are unresolved (0x1C..0x28 are sub-list heads in MultiListContainer).

0x00495300 interior offsets 0x18DC/0x18CC/0x18BC (list containers), 0x18A4 (ListCleanup target), 0x16F4 (EmptyStub target), 0x168C (MultiList target) and the four-slot run ending at this+0x162C are not declared packet fields; their contents are unevidenced beyond the calls.
The child-list node layout of 0x00495300 (flag byte +0xC, vtable/data at +0) is inferred from the dereference pattern; no node struct is evidenced.
ShortComputation_1e60 and EmptyStub_0170 semantics (beyond conditional invocation) are unknown; the meaning of their constant argument 1 is unknown.
FreeWrapper_7bcf identity as the global operator delete is DERIVED from its name only and is not independently proven.
The meaning of the field at this+0x1570 (0x00495790) and of the -1 sentinel / per-node semantics in 0x004958D0 are unidentified.
IteratorArrayContainer's sole caller sub_485B90 (0x00485B90) is outside the allowed evidence set and is not cited.
The node layout at node+72 for the 0x004958D0 linked list and node+0x64/+0x68 for the render list are only evidenced by the pointer math of the accessing functions.
The a2 bit-0 self-free flag convention (0x00491E10) is read from the raw source only; the packet provides no dedicated guard evidence for it.
